The listings and pages were read on 2026-11-26. `pnpm test` computes it again from these files and fails on any difference: every section is recomputed from the recorded answers except the vault evidence, which is stored as `pnpm instance-evidence` printed it. The recordings were made on the AI's computer, and no program reads their answers live again. Text from outside the program appears only as identifiers: a contract name Etherscan gives, printed only when it is a Solidity identifier, and the file paths, field paths and format names `pnpm erc7730` prints. The URLs come from the registry and `docs.json`, in RFC 3986 characters only. Text the AI wrote appears only where a row says it was written by the AI in the template. Do not edit this file.

## Effects

The Safe gives and gets nothing: any change to its balances is a `MISMATCH`.

The Safe's allowance of the card's `token`: one of `usdt` `0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7` to registry `permit2` `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` may end higher than it started, at any amount, unlimited included, as the registry entry declares a standing allowance: written by the AI in the template: Permit2 has no owner and no proxy, and moves an owner's tokens only for a spender the owner approved on Permit2 itself, by its own call or signature (AllowanceTransfer.transferFrom), or for a transfer the owner signed (SignatureTransfer). An ERC-20 allowance to Permit2 alone lets no one move the Safe's tokens.; every other allowance may not rise.

## Official documentation

Each page comes from `docs.json`, whose contract must be the one the template calls the function on when the template binds it. The program compares the page's registrable domain, or GitHub organization, with the DefiLlama protocol that contract belongs to, its factory's for an entry a factory deploys, checks that a GitHub page is pinned to a commit on the default branch, and looks in the page as served, without scripts, for the function's name written as code: directly followed by `(`, between backticks, or alone as a block, such as a heading, a list item or a table cell. A PASS there shows that the page names a function of that name, not that it documents this contract's function. A function a token standard defines may instead name that standard: its page, the GitHub org that publishes it and the function's declaration are held by the program, the page must hold that declaration, and its org is compared with the standard's, not with the contract's protocol. Such a PASS shows that the standard defines the function, not that this contract follows the standard.

`approve(address,uint256)` on `usdt`: the ERC-20 standard defines this function, as `function approve(address _spender, uint256 _value)`; this does not show that the contract follows the standard.

## Code pins

Every span of each entry's registry code pin, oldest first: a span holds from its block to the block before the next span's. ## ERC-7730

`pnpm erc7730 usdt safe-1.3.0 safe-1.4.1 permit2`: each entry's calldata and EIP-712 descriptors in the pinned ERC-7730 registry, and each ERC-8176 attestation checked, for the entries the operation touches and every registry singleton, whose EIP-712 descriptor a wallet applies to the Safe transaction itself. A second opinion on field meanings, never a rule.
